extension.name: Cross-encoder re-ranking over FAISS retrieval, measured before and after on the same workload
extension.evidence: notebooks/06_semantic_search.ipynb and reports/retrieval_metrics.json. Same six answerable test queries, same frozen threshold 0.4592, warm-up excluded from timing. mrr@3 rose from 0.6667 (retrieval only) to 0.7222 after re-ranking the top 6 candidates with cross-encoder/mmarco-mMiniLMv2-L12-H384-v1 — a measured lift of +0.0556. Added cost: median 15.70 ms, p95 17.16 ms per query on CPU. Recall@3 was already 1.0, so the weakness was ordering rather than retrieval, which is exactly what a re-ranker addresses. Decision: ADOPT_FOR_EXPERIMENT, not adoption into the served path — six queries cannot separate the gain from resampling noise, no confidence interval was computed, and the serving path has no latency budget allocated for a second stage. Full adoption is gated on a lift measured on the frozen dataset whose confidence interval excludes zero. Recorded in DECISIONS.md#decision-d-004.
